name: Python Programming
exam: TU assessment: 60% final examination set by the university, 40% internal (assignments, lab work, attendance). Confirm the split in your college's notice.

units.title: Introduction to Python and Basic Elements
topics: Seeing the ideas: the people, the machines and the path of a program

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: the people, the machines and the path of a program

summary: Python is a readable, interpreted, general-purpose language with a rich library; use Python 3.
Variables are names bound to objects; types belong to objects, not names.
Operators follow a precedence table; floats are approximate; use parentheses and tolerances.
Convert types explicitly; format output with f-strings.

units.title: Control Flow
topics: break, continue, pass and loop else
Seeing the ideas: choices, loops and a very long trip

sections.title: break, continue, pass and loop else
Seeing the ideas: choices, loops and a very long trip

summary: if/elif/else and match choose among alternatives; conditions use comparison and logical operators.
while repeats until a condition fails; for iterates over iterables; range generates integer sequences.
break, continue, pass and loop else fine-tune loops; nested loops cost the product of their sizes.
Classic algorithms (primes, GCD, factorial, Fibonacci, digit sums) are all small loops.

units.title: Strings and Built-in Data Structures
topics: Seeing the ideas: text, code points and four containers

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: text, code points and four containers

summary: Strings are immutable sequences with a rich method set; slicing is the universal tool for sequences.
Lists are the general-purpose mutable sequence; comprehensions build them concisely; copies are shallow unless you ask for deep.
Tuples are fixed records, sets give uniqueness and fast membership, dictionaries give key-based lookup.

units.title: Functions, Modules and Packages
topics: Seeing the ideas: bricks, scopes and the call stack

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: bricks, scopes and the call stack

summary: Functions package logic, with flexible parameter passing, scopes that follow LEGB, and first-class function objects.
Recursion, closures, decorators and generators are the building blocks of idiomatic Python.
Modules and packages organise code across files; the standard library covers most everyday tasks.

units.title: File Handling and Exception Handling
topics: Seeing the ideas: records, safety switches and what really happens

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: records, safety switches and what really happens

summary: Files are opened with with, read lazily by iteration, and written with write; pathlib handles paths; csv and json handle structured text.
Exceptions separate normal logic from error handling; try/except/else/finally give precise control, and custom exceptions make errors meaningful.
Handle only what you can handle; let other exceptions propagate.

units.title: Object-Oriented Programming in Python
topics: Seeing the ideas: one mould, many objects

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: one mould, many objects

summary: Classes bundle data and behaviour; objects are instances; self and init are explicit.
Encapsulation in Python is by convention and properties.
Inheritance specialises a class, polymorphism lets code treat different objects uniformly, and abstract classes force a common interface.
Dunder methods integrate your classes with the language; dataclasses and composition keep designs small.

units.title: Data Analysis and Visualisation: NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib
topics: Seeing the ideas: data made visible

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: data made visible

summary: NumPy arrays give fast, vectorised numerical work with broadcasting and built-in statistics and linear algebra.
Pandas turns CSV-style data into DataFrames that can be cleaned, filtered, grouped and merged in a few expressions.
Matplotlib communicates the results as charts.

units.title: Regular Expressions, Databases and Testing
topics: Seeing the ideas: patterns, records, checks and isolation

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: patterns, records, checks and isolation

summary: Regular expressions find and transform text patterns; raw strings and named groups keep them readable.
sqlite3 gives a zero-setup SQL database; parameterised queries stop injection and with con: gives atomic transactions.
Unit tests make change safe; virtual environments keep projects reproducible.

units.title: Putting It Together: Three Complete Programs
topics: Project 3: a small bank in SQLite
Habits of a good Python programmer
Seeing the ideas: from requirements to a working program

sections.title: Project 3: a small bank in SQLite
Habits of a good Python programmer
Seeing the ideas: from requirements to a working program

summary: Small programs combine classes, files, text processing, databases and exceptions; keep the pieces short and independent.
Persistence can be a JSON file for small data or SQLite for structured, transactional data.
Tests, parameterised queries and clear errors turn scripts into dependable software.
